questions.history: Rollback after an explicit flush with primary auto-commit off and target auto-commit on.
questions.prediction: The author reports that the old H2 configuration leaves the row committed. After the merge rollback should complete and the JDBC count for that ID should be zero.
questions.basis: Flush sends the INSERT to the database but does not authorize commit. A fresh connection sees committed state independently of JPA’s first-level cache.
questions.refutation: A rollback exception on H2 or a count of one after merged rollback.

questions.history: With the same pools, insert a different ID, flush and commit normally.
questions.prediction: On both revisions the independent count should be one in the secondary database.
questions.basis: A successful resource-local commit makes the row visible to another connection. It also confirms the query reaches the correct schema.
questions.refutation: The committed row is absent or appears in the primary database.

questions.history: Keep the enabled secondary pool and its database fixed. Vary only primary auto-commit across two runs and use fresh IDs for rollback.
questions.prediction: On the merge both rolled-back IDs should be absent. In both cases `build().getJpaPropertyMap()` should omit `hibernate.connection.provider_disables_autocommit` unless the application overrides it.
questions.basis: Changing a pool which the secondary unit never uses cannot change the secondary transaction’s outcome. The property map and JDBC read test separate boundaries.
questions.refutation: Changing only the primary setting changes the property or leaves a rolled-back row.
